picks.hook_line: Is this 5, 10, 15, 20 years away? — I think it's now. I think we've achieved AGI.
picks.title: Jensen: we've already achieved AGI
picks.why: CEO of the most valuable company says AGI is here, then backs it with the claw-builds-a-viral-app scenario — instant argument-starter.

picks.hook_line: The first job AI researchers said was going to go away was radiology…
picks.title: The AI job prediction that backfired
picks.why: Complete arc: prediction → computer vision did become superhuman → and yet radiologist jobs GREW, now a shortage. Lands right on job-loss anxiety.

picks.hook_line: Do you think about your mortality? Are you afraid of death? — I really don't want to die.
picks.title: Jensen on death
picks.why: Rawest moment of the interview; resolves on 'this is a once-in-humanity experience' — question, confession, and a quotable closer in 40s.

picks.hook_line: The problem was CUDA increased our cost so tremendously it completely consumed all of the company's gross profit dollars.
picks.title: The bet that nearly killed Nvidia
picks.why: Market cap $8B → $1.5B, held the line anyway, 'Nvidia is the house that GeForce built' — a founding-myth story with numbers, exactly 60s.

picks.hook_line: How many people can describe a specification? I think we just went from 30 million to probably 1 billion.
picks.title: From 30 million to 1 billion coders
picks.why: 'Every carpenter will be a coder — and a carpenter with AI is also an architect… I would completely go berserk' — numbers plus an image people repeat.

picks.hook_line: If I have a choice between two new college graduates — one with no clue what AI is, one expert in using AI…
picks.title: Who Jensen would hire today
picks.why: Accountant, lawyer, salesperson — the AI expert wins every time, resolving on 'every college student should graduate an expert in AI'.

picks.hook_line: I don't love continuous improvement — I'd rather strip it all back to zero.
picks.title: 74 days to 6 days
picks.why: Full first-principles arc with a memorable number: '74 days' → 'we can do 72' → strip to zero → 'you'd be surprised, it might come to 6'.

picks.hook_line: I actually think intelligence is a commodity.
picks.title: Intelligence is a commodity
picks.why: Setup and punch in one take: 'they're all superhuman to me — so what is it about a dishwasher that lets him sit in the middle of superhumans?'

picks.hook_line: A CEO told me: Jensen, it's theoretically impossible for a fabless semiconductor company to exceed a billion dollars.
picks.title: Everyone who told Jensen 'impossible'
picks.why: Ladder of wrong predictions ($1B, then $25B) resolving on how to actually think: 'what do we make, and how large is the opportunity we can create'.

picks.hook_line: I've been laying down the bricks… so on the day I announce it, employees say: Jensen, what took you so long?
picks.title: Leading from behind
picks.why: Management insight with a name — shape belief systems daily so big decisions land with 100% buy-in; 'leading from behind' is the payoff phrase.
picks.note: Borderline pick — included to test where the driver's quality floor is.
